raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Every scheduler process initializes tracing, so with TP 8 each request gets eight sets of scheduler spans. The ranks of an attention TP/CP group run the same requests in lockstep, so the copies describe the same batches. They multiply span volume (export cost, collector load, storage) by the group size and crowd the trace view, without adding information for request-level debugging.

This changes a default, so it is kept to one small PR, with an environment variable to restore the previous behavior.

## Modifications

- `should_trace_rank()` in `trace.py` returns true when the process's attention TP rank and attention CP rank are both 0, read from `get_parallel()` (published before `run_scheduler_process` sets up tracing).
- `run_scheduler_process` initializes tracing only when `should_trace_rank()` returns true.
- `SGLANG_TRACE_ALL_RANKS=1` traces every rank, as before, e.g. to debug a rank that diverges.

With DP attention, each DP group keeps its own tracing rank (attention TP rank 0 of the group), and each PP stage keeps one too. A trace context sent to a rank that does not trace arrives disabled, as it already does for any process without tracing (`TraceReqContext.__setstate__`, `TraceReqContextAsync.__setstate__`).

Docs: `SGLANG_TRACE_ALL_RANKS` in `environment_variables.mdx`, and a note under the span-structure diagram in `production_request_trace.mdx`.

### Behavior changes for existing tracing users

- By default only scheduler processes with attention TP rank 0 and attention CP rank 0 export spans; `Scheduler [TP n]` spans for other ranks no longer appear.
- The Mooncake KV transfer worker spans of those other ranks no longer appear either, since they run in the same scheduler process.
- `SGLANG_TRACE_ALL_RANKS=1` restores the previous behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: tracing only, no change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked. With tracing on, scheduler span volume drops by the attention TP × CP group size; with tracing off nothing changes.

## Tests

- New: `test_trace.py::TestShouldTraceRank::test_only_the_first_rank_of_each_attention_group_traces` covers TP rank 1, CP rank 1, and the `SGLANG_TRACE_ALL_RANKS` override.
- Existing: `TestTraceReqContextDisabled::test_setstate_disabled` covers contexts arriving at a process without tracing.
- End to end on 2× L4 (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, TP=2, spans exported to Jaeger): by default only TP rank 0 emitted scheduler spans; after a restart with `SGLANG_TRACE_ALL_RANKS=1`, both ranks did.
- `test/registered/unit/observability`, `managers` and `disaggregation` fail the same tests as `main` and no others.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable: no model-output change.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch: @@ -1118,6 +1118,11 @@ SGLang supports various environment variables that can be used to configure its Config BatchSpanProcessor.max_export_batch_size if tracing is enabled `64` + + `SGLANG_TRACE_ALL_RANKS` + Export scheduler spans from every rank. By default only the first rank of each attention TP/CP group traces + `false` + `SGLANG_TRACE_ASYNC` Enable async tracing: span creation is offloaded to a dedicated exporter process via ZMQ, reducing OTel overhead on the inference hot path

@@ -160,4 +160,6 @@ TraceReqContext (req_id="req-123")
 
 Each traced request maintains a global `TraceReqContext` and creates a corresponding request span. For every thread that processes the request, a `TraceThreadContext` is recorded and a thread span is created. The `TraceThreadContext` is nested within the `TraceReqContext`, and each currently traced code slice—potentially nested—is stored in its associated `TraceThreadContext`.
 
+The ranks of an attention TP/CP group run the same requests in lockstep, so by default only the first rank of each group exports spans (`TP 0` above). Set `SGLANG_TRACE_ALL_RANKS=1` to trace every rank, as in the diagram.
+
 In addition to the above hierarchy, each slice also records its previous slice via Span.add_link(), which can be used to trace the execution flow.
